correctness.rationale: The frozen equation (1) is not the covariance defect for an arbitrary noncentered input: it omits Cov(P(U) mu). For example, with lambda=1, h=1/2, equally likely stages 0 and 1, and input mean and variance both 1, the omitted variance is 1/64. The centred-only argument also did not explain why an arbitrary finite-variance candidate was covered. The full replacement adds the positive-semidefinite term. In an eigenmode t>1 the centered part is strictly positive even without it; t=1 forces U=1, and then every eigenmode must have t=1, giving the identity. For all t_j<1, stationarity of the mean forces zero because each mean multiplier is strictly less than one. Subtracting the covariance constraints for distinct modes then forces E U²=0 and gives a contradiction. In isotropy, bounded Gaussian innovation moments and a uniform multiplier bound below one give the unique stationary law and all finite moments. Its fourth-moment recursion gives (1-E R^4) cumulant_4 = 3 Var(R²/lambda+s); strict monotonicity of q_t makes this positive exactly for nonconstant calibrated stages. The unique deterministic root preserves the full Gaussian by the affine Gaussian update. Equal innovation covariances give the exact point-start W2 factor, and differentiating 2-t-sqrt(1-t²) gives the unique per-step optimum. An independent rational check reproduced the random-stage cumulant 3321/10498, the deterministic stage 5/9 at t=3/5, and a residual 3/49 at the second curvature in a two-mode test. The repair retains the full original classification and fixes its proof for uncentred candidates.
residual_risks: Arithmetic checks are finite; the unrestricted classification and uniqueness depend on the covariance and contraction arguments. The result is not asserted for other noise couplings or separately chosen eigendirection stages.

value.rationale: For a standard explicit randomized midpoint update, a sharp harmonic calibration limit decides when changing the stage law can fix covariance at all. It then distinguishes variance correction from exact sampling and gives the exact best per-step rate among Gaussian-preserving choices. This is valuable for interpreting Gaussian benchmarks without suggesting accuracy for nonlinear potentials or optimality per unit computation or physical time.
